cards.q: What is SMTP and its core role in email?
cards.a: SMTP (TCP 25) is the protocol that sends and relays email between servers; it is a push model where senders push messages onward and clients download their mail via POP3 or IMAP.

cards.q: What are the SMTP port conventions?
cards.a: 25 is the legacy relay/MTA port, 587 is the submission port used with client authentication, and 465 is SMTPS (implicit TLS); modern mail relies on 587 submission and STARTTLS.

cards.q: Where does SMTP fit in the mail delivery path?
cards.a: Client to server submission uses SMTP (25/587), server to server relay uses SMTP (25), and server to client download uses POP3 or IMAP; SMTP is server-to-server and send-side.

cards.q: What does a basic SMTP dialog look like?
cards.a: EHLO greets the server, MAIL FROM: starts the sender, RCPT TO: sets the recipient, DATA begins the message body, a lone period on its own line ends the DATA section, and QUIT closes the session.

cards.q: What are the key SMTP reply codes and the 4xx/5xx rule?
cards.a: 220 ready, 250 OK, 354 start mail input (DATA), 550 mailbox unavailable, and 421/450/451 temporary failures; 5xx codes are permanent failures and 4xx are transient and should be retried later.

cards.q: How is SMTP secured against its classic threats?
cards.a: Open relay abuse is blocked by rejecting non-local RCPT, spoofing is countered with SPF/DKIM/DMARC, cleartext is fixed with STARTTLS and 587 authentication, and password sniffing is prevented with SMTP AUTH over TLS.

cards.q: What is an SMTP open relay and why must it be blocked?
cards.a: An open relay forwards mail from anywhere to anywhere; spammers abuse it to relay spam, so reject non-local recipients.

cards.q: How does SMTP appear in the enterprise networking context?
cards.a: Cisco gear rarely runs SMTP itself since mail gateways/MTAs do, but SNMP traps and syslog reports can ride email via SMTP reporting.

cards.q: What is the practical way to test SMTP manually?
cards.a: A manual telnet mailhost 25 conversation sends SMTP commands and reads server replies to diagnose the service.

cards.q: How do you interpret common SMTP failures?
cards.a: 550 means an invalid recipient (check RCPT address), 421 timeout means the server is busy (retry window), relay denied means open-relay protection is working (check auth and permitted senders), and 4xx means a temporary queue delay.

cards.q: Which retry rule should you remember for SMTP reply codes?
cards.a: 4xx = transient, retry later; 5xx = permanent, do not retry the same thing.
